title: Batuta's aggregated daily summary
description: The ONLY format that leaves the user's machine, and only with explicit opt-in (`batuta config envio sim`). One line per skill per day, produced by `batuta resumo --dia AAAA-MM-DD` (registro.rs, fn resumo_diario). Contains no prompt, prompt hash, turn id, file path, username, IP, or geolocation — if any of these show up in the body, it's a client bug and the ingest rejects it. Field for field identical to what `crates/batuta/src/registro.rs` serializes via `json::escrever` (keys in alphabetical order, no spaces).

schema.description: Format version. If the set of fields changes, the suffix changes — historical series don't get silently patched.

dia.description: Aggregated UTC day (data::dia_utc). UTC, not local timezone: local timezone leaks an approximation of where the person is.

instalacao.description: sha256('instalacao|'+sal)[..16] (casa::id_instalacao). Derived from the local salt: carries no hostname, username, or path. Only serves to say 'these lines came from the same machine'.

batuta_versao.description: CARGO_PKG_VERSION of the binary that generated the line. Without this, comparing days across different versions is comparing different rulers.

modo.description: Where the aggregated data came from. Today the CLI writes 'local'; 'degradado' marks data collected via MCP (§4.1), where there is no hook and the funnel is incomplete.

rotas.description: Turns seen by the router during the day (funnel denominator).

rotas_com_sugestao.description: Turns in which the router spoke. rotas - rotas_com_sugestao = silence (which is a desirable result, not a failure).

rotas_holdout.description: Turns in which the router stayed silent ON PURPOSE (§6). It's the control group; without it, lift measures correlation.

braco_com.description: Outcome of the turns in which the router spoke.

braco_holdout.description: Outcome of the holdout turns. Comparing with braco_com gives the causal lift.

vies_declarado.description: Fixed phrase that travels along with the data (§1.5). The bias doesn't become a footnote on the site: it stays glued to the line.

skills.description: One entry per skill suggested during the day, in alphabetical order (Rust's BTreeMap). Empty is a legitimate response: a day with no routes.

ok.description: Turns judged to have ended well.

n.description: Turns judged in the arm. A small n is reason not to publish a conclusion.

skill.description: Skill name as it appears in the local frontmatter.

versao.description: Version declared by the skill. Empty string when the skill doesn't version itself — and that, in itself, is data about the quality of the ecosystem.

rotas.description: Number of times the router suggested this skill.

ativacoes.description: Number of times the skill actually fired. ativacoes ÷ rotas is the trigger rate (§4.4).

ativacoes_usuario.description: Subset of ativacoes triggered by the user, not by the model (OTEL event claude_code.skill_activated).

turnos_ok.description: turnos_ok ≤ turnos_julgados. The denominator travels along on purpose: a rate without n isn't a number.

reprompts.description: Hard proxy for a bad outcome — doesn't depend on the judge.

custo_usd.description: Sum for the day. Divided by turnos_ok it becomes cost per completed task — the metric nobody else has (§4.4).

turnos_ate_fim_mediana.description: Median, not average: one outlier turn with 40 back-and-forths shouldn't drag the number.

fantasma.description: rotas ≥ 5 and ativacoes = 0. A skill the router keeps suggesting that nobody uses.
